definition: A derivative is a financial contract whose value derives from the price of some other asset (usually referring to an option in practice); the underlying is that other asset used to determine the derivative's price.
core_idea: Derivatives get their value from an underlying asset, and that underlying itself can be another derivative (like a forward or future), including cases where an option references more than one underlying, as with spread options.
key_points: Derivative, in its most general form, is any financial contract whose value is derived from the price of something else.
In practice, the term derivative usually refers to an option.
Underlying is the asset used to determine the price of a derivative.
The underlying can itself be a derivative, such as a forward or a future.
An option can have more than one underlying, as in spread options.
